paragraphs: Yosef, son of Rabbah bar bar Chana.

Hyman reports this in [Yuchasin](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yohasin-zakut/yohasin-zakut09.pdf#page=2) and [Heilprin’s entry on Rav Shmuel](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3352&lang=en): “Yosef and Shmuel, sons of Rabbah bar bar Chana.” He says, “With respect, they erred.” Their source is [Kiddushin 58a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.58a.3-5), which names Rav Yosef (the unqualified Rav Yosef) and Rav Shmuel, “son” of Rabbah bar bar Chana. Mar Yehudah found them and asked a question they could not answer. He came before Rabbah, who said: “Palga’ah, ukminkhi?” [פלגאה אוקמינכי?]. Hyman says he finds no source for Rabbah bar bar Chana having a son named Yosef.[^4]

notes.text: Only Shmuel is identified as Rabbah bar bar Chana’s son in the checked passage. Rashi explains פלגאה as argumentative, not “halves.” Hyman’s singular “he came” differs from the checked plural “they came,” and his concluding quotation is defective; those details remain source questions.

No new primary scalar was returned. Hyman contrasts the quoted works’ plural SONS with singular quoted בריה, SON, modifying only Shmuel; Yosef is the unqualified Rav Yosef. His accusation of error and statement that no such son is found remain HIS claims, not a new corpus-wide negative result. The earlier Kiddushin consultation has THEY came against supplied HE came; the supplied singular is retained. The concluding פלגאה אוקמינכי? remains explicit and uncertain rather than a confident reconstructed quotation. The earlier Rashi explanation of palga’ah as argumentative is inherited, not newly inspected. רבב״ח is a conventional contextual expansion; its separate heading does not assert a real Yosef genealogy.

In the consulted Yuchasin (London 1857, p. 146), the notice about Mar Yehudah calls both men sons of Rabbah bar bar Chana, places the visit before Rava, and makes Mar Yehudah the target of the rebuke. Seder HaDorot also calls Yosef the brother of Shmuel in the notice under Rav Shmuel (3352:1), while its entry on Mar Yehudah (1707:1) records the singular “son” attached to Shmuel. In Kiddushin 58a the visitors come before Rabbah in the plural. The text reads אוקמינכו and has Rabbah say that someone put them up to the question. Rashi glosses פלגא as a person given to disputing with his colleagues. Hyman’s singular narration and the spelling אוקמינכי are retained as printed.

[Heilprin’s entry on Mar Yehudah](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1707&lang=en) places “son” after Shmuel. At the end of the linked Kiddushin passage, Rabbah says that a quarrelsome person put them up to the question. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Kiddushin.58a.5.1) takes the first word to mean someone in the habit of disputing with his colleagues.
